name: OPTUMSERVE HEALTH SERVICES, INC.
agency: Department of Health and Human Services
naics_description: ALL OTHER MISCELLANEOUS AMBULATORY HEALTH CARE SERVICES
brief_text:
Four detectors flagged OptumServe Health Services. Modification growth showed the most extreme signal: a single parent contract grew by a factor of 429 times, roughly 36 standard deviations above peers in the same industry code. Sole-source concentration also fired strongly, with 67 percent of awards issued without competition compared to a median of zero percent among 42 comparable ambulatory health care providers. The isolation detector identified the entity as a multivariate outlier based on its combination of high dollar volume, award frequency, and modification patterns. Benford's law analysis of leading digits in award amounts showed no statistical anomaly.

The worst contract, HT001119D0002, grew at a ratio of 428.71 against a peer average of 12.00, yielding a z-score of 10.998. OptumServe received 24 sole-source awards out of 36 total, a rate 4.51 standard deviations above the peer median. The entity accumulated 548.7 million dollars across 36 awards, with 89 percent of awards modified and work spanning five NAICS codes across two agencies.

These signals reflect statistical extremes within the ambulatory health care services sector, but context matters. OptumServe is a large, established subsidiary of a major health services corporation, which may legitimately explain high modification frequency and sole-source awards in specialized health services delivery. The peer group of 42 entities may include smaller or differently structured providers, limiting direct comparability. Modification growth and sole-source concentration warrant closer review of contract justifications and pricing, but neither signal alone proves misconduct.
